title: Artificial Analysis v5 and the benchmarker's dilemma
author: Nathan Lambert
description: A sort of review of the benchmarking industry and what's missing.
summary: Hill-climbing is easy, knowing what to hill-climb is hard. Making scores go up is expensive , but we have a much clearer playbook for it than we do for creating meaningful benchmarks at the true frontier of AI today.
takeaways: Some other benchmarks measure certain skills that will be needed of a model in repetitive agentic tasks.

This is an okay decision to take, but over time as existing workflows of open models become key factors of the economy, it could become a benchmark that misses where the core economic engine of the industry is.

Consider this plot from the Kimi K3.1 Pro launch — yes, the open models are strong and useful in some cases, but the best OpenAI and Anthropic models have been a major step ahead in their flexibility and reliability.
